subject: Mid-cycle OKR health, trade-offs, and dependency wishlist
messages:
From: Avery Johnson <avery@redwood.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.ai>
Cc: leadership@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 4 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Mid-cycle OKR health, trade-offs, and dependency wishlist

Team —

Posting a short mid-cycle health note for our QBR prep. I pulled the data from the console dashboards and spoke with product pods this week. High-level signal: we are on track on three priority KR buckets, but two areas need explicit trade-offs or extra capacity to meet the end-of-quarter targets.

Summary (topline):
- Serving runtime throughput (KR: reduce avg p95 latency by 15%): green for baseline workloads, amber for long-sequence requests impacting smaller pods.
- Cost-per-inference (KR: -12% unit cost): behind pace because of unoptimized quantization rollout and several models still on higher memory backends.
- Rollout & Coverage (KR: expand model catalog): on track for curated list; slower for private deployments due to customer-specific infra gates.

Concrete asks / proposed trade-offs:
1) Shift two backend infra engineers from feature X (infra backlog) to the quantization sprint for the next 3 weeks. Expected impact: ~7% unit cost improvement by EoQ.
2) Accept a temporary scope trim on the long-seq optimization work (defer advanced attention kernel 2.0) to preserve latency SLA for 95% of traffic.
3) Fast-track three customer private deployment requests by offering a Dedicated pilot (limited scope, higher price) to avoid blocking the KR for private deployments.

Dependencies (wishlist):
- Priority access to extra Dedicated capacity (1x A100 node pool) for a 2-week window during model retrain and quantization testing.
- Quick legal sign-off on a narrow Dedicated pilot agreement template (see attached deck).
- Procurement engagement to confirm accelerated invoicing for pilot customers (Acme is first).

I've attached a short readout deck and a CSV with prioritized dependency asks. Can each of you reply with: (a) whether you can commit headcount shift (yes/no + who), (b) whether you endorse the scope trim, and (c) any procurement/legal blockers we should escalate now.

Thanks — this will inform the leadership QBR slide and the canary rollout plan.

— Avery
Avery Johnson
Director, Product Ops | Redwood Inference
avery@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0134

Attachments: QBR-readout-deck-v1.2.pdf (slide deck, 8 slides) ; dependency-wishlist.csv (spreadsheet)
From: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.ai>
To: Avery Johnson <avery@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 4 Sep 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Mid-cycle OKR health, trade-offs, and dependency wishlist

Thanks for the crisp note, Avery. Quick responses below.

1) Headcount: I can spare one infra engineer (Diego) for the quantization sprint for the next 2 weeks (not 3) — beyond that we risk stalling some infra backlog tickets that affect production stability. If Laura can free another backend by week 2 we can extend to three weeks.

2) Scope trim: I agree with deferring attention kernel 2.0 for now. Let's gate the decision on a simple SLA check: if any customer hits >300ms p95 on long sequences, we re-open.

3) Dedicated pilot: I support the pilot but want a clear rollback policy and cost accounting. Procurement/legal should get the pilot template early; Naomi can you flag any non-negotiables?

Also: I'll provision a 1x A100 temporary pool this afternoon (best-effort) and add logs so we can correlate latency improvements.

— Markus
Markus Klein
VP, Infrastructure | Redwood Inference
markus@redwood.ai

- Dedicated pilot for private deployments: Owner = Naomi (Customer Ops) for templated terms; Sales to draft the pilot pricing and acceptance criteria (I'll cc Sales in follow-up).
